# `Q-2-53` — Fenced div info string starts with `-`

> The word after a fenced div's opening colons starts with `-`, which
> Quarto 2 reserves for the block deletion mark `::: --`.

## What this means

A fenced div opens with a line of three or more colons. The colons can
be followed by a single bare word, which becomes the div's class
(`::: note` is `<div class="note">`), or by an attribute block
(`::: {.note #intro}`).

In Quarto 2, the bare word cannot start with `-`. After the colons, a
leading `-` is reserved for **editorial marks**. `::: --` opens a block
whose content is marked as deleted. It is the block form of the inline
`[-- deleted text]`. The marks `::: ++` (inserted), `::: >>` (comment)
and `::: !!` (highlighted) work the same way.

So `::: --foo`, `::: ---` and `::: -x` are errors, not divs.

## Why this happens

- **A block deletion mark with no space after it.** `::: --` has to be
  followed by a space, the end of the line, or an attribute block
  (`::: --{author="me"}`). `::: --draft` is read as an attempt to name
  a class `--draft`.
- **A document written for Quarto 1 or Pandoc.** Both read `::: --foo`
  as a div with class `--foo`. A class name starting with dashes is
  unusual, and we have not found one in practice. If you do use one,
  it now has to be set as an attribute.

## How to fix

To mark the content as deleted, put a space or a line break after the
two dashes:

```markdown
::: --

This paragraph is marked as deleted.

:::
```

To use a class whose name starts with `-`, set it with a `class`
attribute (the `.name` shorthand does not accept a leading `-` either):

```markdown
::: {class="--foo"}

Content.

:::
```

Better still, rename the class so that it starts with a letter:
`::: foo` or `::: {.foo}`.
